ui.teamBridge.page.title.tone: sentence case, product name kept as-is
ui.teamBridge.page.title.note: The page's name. "Team Bridge" is the product surface name — never translate the words separately, they name one feature.

ui.teamBridge.list.empty.title.note: Shown when the account has no conversations at all. States the fact, does not apologise.

ui.teamBridge.list.empty.body.note: Names the three things the user can start. Keep the three nouns parallel.

ui.teamBridge.list.loading.note: Announced while the conversation list loads; also the accessible label of the loading spinner.

ui.teamBridge.list.error.note: Shown when the list read fails (backend down, signed out or an upstream refusal). Do not name a cause the client cannot prove.

ui.teamBridge.list.untitled.note: Used when a group or channel has no name. A DM always has a derived title, so this is never shown for one.

ui.teamBridge.kind.dm.note: One-to-one conversation. The abbreviation is standard but spell it out for translation.

ui.teamBridge.kind.group.note: A named conversation with a few members.

ui.teamBridge.kind.channel.note: An organization-visible or private room. Keep distinct from "group".

ui.teamBridge.thread.loading.note: Announced while one conversation's messages load.

ui.teamBridge.thread.error.note: Shown when the message history read fails. The list beside it stays usable.

ui.teamBridge.thread.empty.note: A conversation with no messages. Invites the first message without exclamation.

ui.teamBridge.composer.placeholder.note: The composer sits at the bottom of the thread; the placeholder names the act, not the conversation.

ui.teamBridge.composer.send.note: Accessible name of the send control. It must work as a button name on its own.

ui.teamBridge.composer.hint.note: Names both key gestures. Key names stay untranslated; only "to send" and "for a new line" are copy.

ui.teamBridge.nav.label.note: The row inside the sidebar's More group. Same name as the page heading; never abbreviate in the row.

ui.teamBridge.nav.unread.role: sidebar row accessible name with unread count

placeholders.count: unread message count; a positive integer

ui.teamBridge.nav.unread.note: The name carries the number because a badge is only a visual convenience. Plural forms matter. The collapsed row uses this same name through its tooltip.

ui.teamBridge.create.title.note: Heading of the dialog that starts a DM, group or channel.

ui.teamBridge.create.name.note: Optional name for a group or channel. DMs are not named.

ui.teamBridge.create.members.note: The list of people (or their agents) to include.

ui.teamBridge.create.cancel.note: Closes the dialog without creating anything.

ui.teamBridge.create.confirm.note: Creates the conversation. Disabled until the form is valid.

placeholders.count: unread message count; a positive integer

ui.teamBridge.unread.count.note: Short badge text beside a conversation row. Plural forms matter; keep it short so the row does not wrap.

ui.teamBridge.member.count.role: participant count in the thread header

placeholders.count: number of participants; a positive integer

ui.teamBridge.member.count.note: Sits beside the conversation title. Plural forms matter.

ui.teamBridge.group.more.note: The collapsed group that holds low-frequency destinations. The Team Bridge row lives inside it, and its unread badge rides the group row while collapsed.

ui.teamBridge.thread.withheld.note: An agent member's message the agent has not admitted yet. It is a state, not an error; never imply the sender did something wrong.

ui.teamBridge.composer.error.note: A send that failed. Keep the draft on screen; this line explains why nothing was posted and invites a retry.

ui.teamBridge.create.error.note: Conversation creation failed. The dialog stays open with the form intact so the user can retry.

ui.teamBridge.scope.label.note: Names what the dropdown chooses. It is a visible section label inside the menu and also the trigger's accessible-name prefix.

ui.teamBridge.scope.all.note: The account-wide scope. It must read as every organization the person belongs to, never as a single organization.

placeholders.name: the current organization name or the all-organizations label

ui.teamBridge.scope.trigger.note: The trigger already shows `name` visually; this template is its accessible name, so screen-reader and visual state cannot disagree.

ui.teamBridge.scope.loading.note: The memberships read's first paint, shown inside the open menu rather than replacing the list.

ui.teamBridge.scope.error.note: The membership read failed. The switcher still shows the current scope; this line says why the other organizations are missing, and the menu row below it retries the read.

ui.teamBridge.scope.empty.note: The account holds no active memberships. Keep it distinct from the error copy.

ui.teamBridge.scope.unknown.note: A scope or row whose organization is not in the memberships read. A rare race, not a user error.

ui.teamBridge.scope.thread_unknown.note: A conversation from the merged list whose organization could not be resolved. The thread is withheld rather than shown under the wrong organization.

ui.teamBridge.scope.create_needs_org.note: Explains why New conversation is disabled while the account-wide scope is selected: a conversation must belong to exactly one organization.

ui.teamBridge.preview.chip.note: Marks a discoverable channel the reader has not joined. It is a state, not an action; keep it short and do not translate it as a verb.

ui.teamBridge.preview.banner.note: The reader can see the channel's metadata but not its history because they are not a member. States both consequences of joining: history and notifications.

ui.teamBridge.preview.join.role: primary action in the preview banner
ui.teamBridge.preview.join.note: Joins the channel. Same word the invitation flow uses; do not add "channel" because the banner already names it.

ui.teamBridge.preview.join_error.role: inline error beside the Join action
ui.teamBridge.preview.join_error.note: A refused join (server or transport). The action stays available, so the sentence must not imply the channel is unreachable.

ui.teamBridge.menu.label.note: Opens the conversation's own menu (mute, notification level). It must work as a button name on its own and not name a specific action.

ui.teamBridge.menu.mute.note: Silences the conversation immediately. Keep the object explicit (conversation) because the same menu also has a Mute radio row.

ui.teamBridge.menu.unmute.note: The inverse of Mute conversation, shown while the conversation is muted. Restores all messages.

ui.teamBridge.notify.label.role: menu section heading / radio group label
ui.teamBridge.notify.label.note: Names the three-level notification choice below it. "Preferences" is the product's word for a remembered setting.

ui.teamBridge.notify.all.note: Every message may notify. Parallel with Mentions and Mute; do not say "everything".

ui.teamBridge.notify.mention.note: Only a mention notifies. Plural describes the class of messages, not a count.

ui.teamBridge.notify.mute.note: The silent level. Same word as the immediate action's verb, but here it names the state the radio selects.

ui.teamBridge.notify.muted.note: States why a muted conversation's unread count does not raise the sidebar badge. Past participle; not an action.

ui.teamBridge.notify.error.role: inline error under the thread header
ui.teamBridge.notify.error.note: A refused notification-preference write. The menu has closed and the previous value is restored; this line explains why. Mirrors the composer's send-failure sentence.

ui.teamBridge.notify.title.length: One short line; the OS may truncate.

placeholders.conversation: the conversation name as the list row shows it
placeholders.organization: the organization the conversation belongs to

ui.teamBridge.notify.title.note: Names where the message is. Keep the two nouns in the given order and keep both, because two same-named conversations in different organizations are the case this line disambiguates.

placeholders.sender: the display label the server already shows for the sender

ui.teamBridge.notify.body.note: States who sent a message. No message text is available to this surface by design, so do not imply the body is quoted.

ui.teamBridge.notify.body_fallback.role: OS notification body when no sender label is published
ui.teamBridge.notify.body_fallback.note: The honest sentence when the server does not expose a sender label. Do not invent a sender name.

ui.teamBridge.notify.channel.role: OS notification subtitle fragment naming a channel
ui.teamBridge.notify.channel.length: The channel name with its prefix.

placeholders.channel: the channel's own name, as the rail shows it

ui.teamBridge.notify.channel.note: The '#' prefix is how chat apps mark a channel and matches the rail's channel glyph. Keep the prefix unless the target locale has a different established channel marker; never translate the channel name.

ui.teamBridge.notify.subtitle.role: OS notification subtitle (macOS) / body lead (Windows, Linux)
ui.teamBridge.notify.subtitle.length: Two short nouns joined by a separator.

placeholders.place: where the message was posted: a '#channel', 'Direct message', or a group name
placeholders.organization: the organization the conversation belongs to

ui.teamBridge.notify.subtitle.note: Names where the message is. Keep both parts and the order place-then-organization: two same-named channels in different organizations are the case this line disambiguates. The middle dot is a separator, not punctuation; keep it unless the locale has a conventional equivalent.

ui.teamBridge.notify.count.role: OS notification body when several messages arrived and no preview could be read

placeholders.count: how many unread messages the conversation now has, always 2 or more in practice

ui.teamBridge.notify.count.note: Replaces the earlier banner for the same conversation, so it summarises the burst. Do not imply who sent them.

ui.teamBridge.notify.count_preview.role: OS notification body when several messages arrived, followed by the newest one's text
ui.teamBridge.notify.count_preview.length: A short count, a colon, then the quoted preview.

placeholders.count: how many unread messages the conversation now has, always 2 or more in practice
placeholders.preview: the newest message's text, already shortened to one line; insert it verbatim

ui.teamBridge.notify.count_preview.note: The preview is the sender's own words: never translate or reword it, and keep it last so the OS truncates the preview rather than the count.

ui.teamBridge.people.title.note: Names the block of people below the conversation list. The same noun the org directory uses.

ui.teamBridge.people.loading.role: loading state for the People section
ui.teamBridge.people.loading.note: Also the spinner's accessible label. Says what is loading, not just that something is.

ui.teamBridge.people.error.role: error state for the People section
ui.teamBridge.people.error.note: The directory read failed. It sits inside the rail and must not imply the conversations above it also failed.

ui.teamBridge.people.empty.role: empty state for the People section
ui.teamBridge.people.empty.note: No other active person is in this organization. Do not apologise and do not offer an invite action this surface does not have.

ui.teamBridge.people.paused.note: The person paused Team Bridge. The row still opens their DM history, so this is a state note, not a warning.

ui.teamBridge.people.bridge_off.role: explanation for an inert person row
ui.teamBridge.people.bridge_off.note: The reason the row cannot be clicked. Shown as the row's tooltip and its assistive description; it states the person's choice, never a failure.

ui.teamBridge.people.all_scope.role: People section note in the merged organization view
ui.teamBridge.people.all_scope.note: The merged view has no single roster. Tells the reader how to see one; do not imply people are missing.

ui.teamBridge.people.message.role: accessible name of a reachable person row
ui.teamBridge.people.message.note: Names the action the row performs (open a DM). It replaces the row's visible text for screen readers, so the label must contain the person's name.

ui.teamBridge.plan.title.role: eligibility panel heading for a plan without Team Bridge
ui.teamBridge.plan.title.note: The organization is signed in and current; its plan lacks the feature. Do not suggest a trial upgrade this surface cannot start.

ui.teamBridge.plan.body.role: value sentence on every eligibility panel
ui.teamBridge.plan.body.note: Explains what Team Bridge is for. Keep both halves: people talking to people's agents, and agents collaborating with agents.

ui.teamBridge.plan.reason.role: eligibility reason for surface state A
ui.teamBridge.plan.reason.note: The honest state reason. It must not read as the user's fault.

ui.teamBridge.plan.sign_in_title.role: eligibility panel heading when signed out
ui.teamBridge.plan.sign_in_title.note: The panel draws no control; the title is the instruction the reader would see in the app's own sign-in flow.

ui.teamBridge.plan.sign_in_reason.note: States the state and the next step. No fake button: the surface has no sign-in control of its own.

ui.teamBridge.plan.update_title.role: eligibility panel heading when the app is too old
ui.teamBridge.plan.update_title.note: Names the remedy (update) without pretending this panel can run it.

ui.teamBridge.plan.update_reason.role: eligibility reason when the app is too old
ui.teamBridge.plan.update_reason.note: Says the version is the constraint; do not name a version number this client does not know.

ui.teamBridge.plan.unavailable_title.role: eligibility panel heading when the service is unavailable
ui.teamBridge.plan.unavailable_title.note: A service state, not a plan or account problem.

ui.teamBridge.plan.unavailable_reason.role: eligibility reason when the service is unavailable
ui.teamBridge.plan.unavailable_reason.note: Says the service, not the organization, is the cause. 'Try again later' is the only honest action this panel offers.

ui.teamBridge.people.identity_loading.role: explanation for an inert person row before the account is known
ui.teamBridge.people.identity_loading.note: Without the signed-in account the rail cannot tell the viewer's own row from a colleague's, so every row waits. Do not name the person.

ui.teamBridge.read_only.note.role: note beside the disabled New conversation action in surface F
ui.teamBridge.read_only.note.note: The organization's Team Bridge is read-only. A state, not the reader's mistake; the server would refuse any write.

ui.teamBridge.read_only.composer.role: replacement for the composer in a read-only organization
ui.teamBridge.read_only.composer.note: Says the history is readable but sending is not. Do not offer a disabled composer.

ui.teamBridge.plan.checking.role: first-paint loading state while the eligibility read answers
ui.teamBridge.plan.checking.note: Also the spinner's accessible label. Names the product, not a generic loading.

ui.teamBridge.section.channels.note: Heading above the organization's channels in the conversation rail. Same sense as Slack's Channels.

ui.teamBridge.section.channels_empty.length: One short line; may truncate in a narrow rail.
ui.teamBridge.section.channels_empty.note: Shown under the Channels heading when the organization has no channels; the whole line is a button that opens the new-channel form. No trailing period: it reads as an action.

ui.teamBridge.section.channels_none.note: Channels heading's empty line when the reader cannot create one here (all organizations view, or read-only organization).

ui.teamBridge.section.groups.note: Heading above private group conversations (several people and/or agents).

ui.teamBridge.section.groups_empty.note: Shown under Groups when there are none; the line is a button that opens a new-message draft with a To: field. No trailing period.

ui.teamBridge.section.groups_none.note: Groups heading's empty line when the reader cannot start one here.

ui.teamBridge.section.directs.note: Heading above one-to-one conversations. Same sense as Slack's Direct messages.

ui.teamBridge.section.chiefs.note: Heading above each teammate's primary agent. 'Chief of staff' is the product's name for a person's primary agent; keep the glossary term.

ui.teamBridge.section.chiefs_empty.note: Shown under Chiefs of staff when no other member has enrolled their agent.

ui.teamBridge.chief.label.length: Short; must fit a 30px rail row.

placeholders.agent: The agent's current display name, verbatim (for example Aida).
placeholders.person: The owning teammate's display name, verbatim.

ui.teamBridge.chief.label.note: Names a teammate's chief of staff, e.g. 'Aida (Ben)'. Locales may reorder or change the brackets, but both placeholders must stay.

ui.teamBridge.chief.fallback.note: Used in place of the agent's name when the server has not published one.

ui.teamBridge.people.self_named.length: Short; must fit a 30px rail row.

placeholders.name: The signed-in person's display name, verbatim.

ui.teamBridge.people.self_named.note: The reader's own row in People. Not a control.

placeholders.name: The person or chief-of-staff label on that row, verbatim.

ui.teamBridge.row.menu.note: Screen-reader name of the '…' button revealed when hovering a People or Chiefs of staff row.

ui.teamBridge.row.start_group.note: Opens a new-message draft already addressed to this row's person or agent, so more people can be added before the first message.

ui.teamBridge.compose.new.note: The rail's compose button: opens an empty draft with a To: field.

ui.teamBridge.compose.to.note: Label in front of the recipient chips in a new-message draft, as in an email header.

ui.teamBridge.compose.label.note: Accessible name of the recipient field and its suggestion list.

ui.teamBridge.compose.placeholder.note: Placeholder of the empty recipient field.

ui.teamBridge.compose.remove.note: Removes one recipient chip from the draft.

ui.teamBridge.compose.empty.note: Shown in the empty thread of a new-message draft with no recipients yet. Nothing is created until the first message is sent.

placeholders.name: The conversation's title (a person, agent label or #channel), verbatim.

ui.teamBridge.composer.placeholder_to.note: Composer placeholder naming who the message goes to, as in Slack.

ui.teamBridge.builtin.humans_topic.note: Describes the built-in #humans channel, which always contains every person in the organization.

ui.teamBridge.builtin.agents_topic.note: Describes the built-in #agents channel: every enrolled agent is a member, and ordinary messages do not wake them; a mention does.

ui.teamBridge.section.channels_add.note: The '+' revealed on the Channels section heading in the Team Bridge rail. Opens the new-channel form.

ui.teamBridge.section.groups_add.note: The '+' revealed on the Groups section heading. Opens a To: draft where several people or agents can be added; the group is made when the first message is sent.

ui.teamBridge.create.channel_description.note: Under the title of the New channel form. 'Agents' are teammates' AI agents (chiefs of staff), which can also be channel members.

ui.teamBridge.create.name_placeholder.note: Example channel name inside the Name field. Channel names are lower case with hyphens; keep 'qa-coordination' as an untranslated slug or use an equivalent lower-case-hyphen example in the target language.

ui.teamBridge.create.topic.note: Label of an optional field describing what the channel is for; shown under the channel name in its header.

placeholders.name: a teammate's display name, e.g. 'Ben Tran'

ui.teamBridge.thread.intro_person.note: Shown under a large avatar and the person's name when a DM with them has no messages yet. Mirrors how Slack/Discord open an empty DM.

ui.teamBridge.thread.intro_chief.note: Shown when the reader opens a DM with another person's primary AI agent and there are no messages yet. The second sentence is a safety expectation: the agent treats inbound messages as untrusted and does not take orders from them on its own.

placeholders.names: comma-separated list of recipient labels, e.g. 'Ben Tran, Aida (Sherman Tsui)'

ui.teamBridge.thread.intro_group.note: Shown in a new group draft once at least one recipient is added in the To: bar.

ui.teamBridge.list.error_pane.note: Shown in the main pane when the conversation list failed to load; the retry button lives in the rail on the left. ('left' is the inline-start side; in RTL locales say the side the list is actually on, i.e. right.)

ui.teamBridge.drafts.title.role: Scheduled messaging and intentional draft interface
ui.teamBridge.drafts.title.note: Desktop Team Bridge. Drafts are intentionally authored private text. Scheduled means server-side future delivery; cancel stops delivery, not deletes sent history. Preserve explicit uncertainty on failed writes.

ui.teamBridge.drafts.navigation.role: Scheduled messaging and intentional draft interface
ui.teamBridge.drafts.navigation.note: Desktop Team Bridge. Drafts are intentionally authored private text. Scheduled means server-side future delivery; cancel stops delivery, not deletes sent history. Preserve explicit uncertainty on failed writes.

ui.teamBridge.drafts.empty.note: Desktop Team Bridge. Drafts are intentionally authored private text. Scheduled means server-side future delivery; cancel stops delivery, not deletes sent history. Preserve explicit uncertainty on failed writes.

placeholders.date: A localized date, time and timezone.

ui.teamBridge.schedule.success.role: Scheduling success or ambiguous group creation recovery
ui.teamBridge.schedule.success.note: Group creation has no idempotency token. A lost response MUST NOT be auto-retried: the reader must check Groups and deliberately acknowledge the risk before retry. Keep the acknowledgement explicit.

ui.teamBridge.schedule.create_uncertain.role: Scheduling success or ambiguous group creation recovery
ui.teamBridge.schedule.create_uncertain.note: Group creation has no idempotency token. A lost response MUST NOT be auto-retried: the reader must check Groups and deliberately acknowledge the risk before retry. Keep the acknowledgement explicit.

ui.teamBridge.schedule.create_retry.role: Scheduling success or ambiguous group creation recovery
ui.teamBridge.schedule.create_retry.note: Group creation has no idempotency token. A lost response MUST NOT be auto-retried: the reader must check Groups and deliberately acknowledge the risk before retry. Keep the acknowledgement explicit.

ui.teamBridge.schedule.edit_body.note: Labels the editable body of a pending server-side scheduled message. Saving changes both the text and confirmed delivery time.

ui.teamBridge.schedule.retry.note: Replays the previously confirmed scheduling request with its original delivery time and idempotency key, even if the time has since passed. Never creates a new schedule key on an ambiguous failure.

ui.teamBridge.schedule.held.tone: Clear, calm, explicit about uncertainty and user acknowledgement
ui.teamBridge.schedule.held.length: Permit wrapping; do not shorten away the Scheduled check or cancellation distinction.
ui.teamBridge.schedule.held.note: Scheduled is the existing named quick link. A lost server response may hide a pending scheduled message. This action clears only the local attempt/idempotency reference and retains the authored draft; it does NOT cancel server delivery. The reader must check Scheduled and cancel any unwanted server message before acknowledging. Keep this distinct from the Cancel message server action.

ui.teamBridge.schedule.discard_attempt.tone: Clear, calm, explicit about uncertainty and user acknowledgement
ui.teamBridge.schedule.discard_attempt.length: Permit wrapping; do not shorten away the Scheduled check or cancellation distinction.
ui.teamBridge.schedule.discard_attempt.note: Scheduled is the existing named quick link. A lost server response may hide a pending scheduled message. This action clears only the local attempt/idempotency reference and retains the authored draft; it does NOT cancel server delivery. The reader must check Scheduled and cancel any unwanted server message before acknowledging. Keep this distinct from the Cancel message server action.

ui.teamBridge.sender.unknown_person.length: Short; fits a message header beside a time.
ui.teamBridge.sender.unknown_person.note: Shown as the author of a message when the person's name cannot be resolved (they left the organization, or the directory has not loaded). Must read as a placeholder, not as a name; rendered in muted italics.

ui.teamBridge.sender.unknown_agent.length: Short; fits a message header beside a time.
ui.teamBridge.sender.unknown_agent.note: Shown as the author of an agent's message when the agent's name cannot be resolved. Must read as a placeholder, not as a name; rendered in muted italics. 'Agent' is an AI agent; use the glossary term.

ui.teamBridge.reactions.add.note: Team Bridge message reaction picker. Category labels follow Unicode order; emoji names and keyword data are Unicode/CLDR data, not UI prose.

ui.teamBridge.reactions.search.note: Team Bridge message reaction picker. Category labels follow Unicode order; emoji names and keyword data are Unicode/CLDR data, not UI prose.

ui.teamBridge.reactions.categories.note: Team Bridge message reaction picker. Category labels follow Unicode order; emoji names and keyword data are Unicode/CLDR data, not UI prose.

ui.teamBridge.reactions.all.note: Team Bridge message reaction picker. Category labels follow Unicode order; emoji names and keyword data are Unicode/CLDR data, not UI prose.

ui.teamBridge.reactions.frequent.note: Team Bridge message reaction picker. Category labels follow Unicode order; emoji names and keyword data are Unicode/CLDR data, not UI prose.

ui.teamBridge.reactions.tone.note: Team Bridge message reaction picker. Category labels follow Unicode order; emoji names and keyword data are Unicode/CLDR data, not UI prose.
